# `kernel/execution/DodadForge.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/execution/DodadForge.js`

DodadForge.js — OS-owned project contracts for interactive AI Echo outputs. Provider text is never executed directly. The forge accepts either one complete self-contained document or a manifest-driven local file graph, validates it as data, and runs declared behavior only in an opaque, network-blocked iframe before the existing signed Dodad Faculty is allowed to persist the project. The strict four-file profile remains only as a backward-compatible authoring/update reader for existing Engine package-v1 graphs; it is never the default shape for new work.

### `createDodadProjectDraftProjector()`

Incrementally expose a manifest-driven project as inert per-file previews. No provider path is trusted until the complete manifest is valid. Invalid or incomplete manifests never create arbitrary preview entries, and projected bytes never enter persistence or runtime admission.

### `normalizeDodadDraftPreview(value)`

Normalize one quarantined preview for UI projection. This is deliberately shared with the canonical Forge so the UI cannot impose a second, older file-layout contract. Returned bytes remain ephemeral and non-executable.

### `normalizeDodadForgeProviderProject(input = {}, envelopeEvidence = null)`

Apply only deterministic, semantics-preserving provider-envelope repairs. Direct validation remains strict so callers can distinguish authored input from the exact bytes that are eligible for runtime verification and saving.

### `resolveDodadEngineDemoRuntimeProfile(value)`

Resolve one reviewed, locally packageable Engine Demo runtime profile.

### `validateDodadEngineDemoContract({ html = '', javascript = '', manifest = null } = {})`

Validate the extra contract required by the engine-demo recipe. This is intentionally a pure static gate. It proves that authored code is bound to the OS-supplied verified runtime and contains the lifecycle seams a dedicated Engine Demo preview/export host needs. It does not claim that GPU execution occurred in the ordinary opaque Dodad verifier.

Deterministic quality projection; blockers cover recipe-defining behavior only.

### `async verifyDodadJavaScriptWorker(source, { timeoutMs = WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS } = {})`

Parse the Dodad's JavaScript inside a killable Worker. Authored source is transferred as data to a fixed trusted bootstrap and is never invoked in the Worker's same-origin realm.

### `discoverDodadBehaviorManifest(files)`

Discover the one behavior authority from its reviewed content identity. Filenames are intentionally irrelevant in modular projects. Zero or more than one matching JSON object is ambiguous and therefore never admitted.

### `discoverDodadBehaviorAuthority(files, { entrypoint = '' } = {})`

Discover one behavior-test authority without prescribing a file layout. A modular graph may keep the reviewed JSON in a support file. A complete single HTML Dodad may instead embed the identical inert JSON payload in one `<script type="application/json" data-dodad-behavior>` element. The element is data, is removed by the opaque runtime builder, and is never executable.

### `normalizeDodadProjectBase(value, { allowMissingSingleDocumentAuthority = false, } = {})`

### `inspectDodadJavaScriptCapabilities(value, options = {})`

Content-free callers may use the same reviewed capability scanner for one staged source unit before the complete project crosses final validation.

### `isReviewedDodadRepairReason(value)`

Whether a stable local failure class has an exact, content-free repair.

### `isReviewedRepeatedDodadValidationFailure(result, priorReasonCodes = [])`

Whether a repaired provider route repeated only failures already disclosed through the reviewed, content-free repair contract. This predicate is deliberately narrower than general repair eligibility. It admits only local static-validation failures, requires every bounded failure string to map to a reviewed prior reason, and rejects mixed known/unknown evidence. Callers may then try another already-approved provider route with the same history-free prompt; every candidate still crosses full admission.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
